questions.question:
[대화]
A : Welcome to Delicious Snack. Are you ready to order?
B : Yes, I want a hot dog and an egg sandwich, please.
A : Will that be all?
B : No. I'd like to order two bottles of water.
A : Is it for here or to go?
B : It's for here, please.
A : The total comes to 15 dollars.
B : OK. Here you are.

밑줄 친 부분의 의도로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: "Will that be all?"은 고객이 주문을 완료했는지 확인하고 추가로 더 주문할 것이 있는지를 묻는 표현이므로 '추가 주문 확인'이 정답입니다.

options: Somi는 핫도그와 계란 샌드위치, 물을 각 하나씩 주문했다.
questions.question:
[대화]
A : Welcome to Delicious Snack. Are you ready to order?
B : Yes, I want a hot dog and an egg sandwich, please.
A : Will that be all?
B : No. I'd like to order two bottles of water.
A : Is it for here or to go?
B : It's for here, please.
A : The total comes to 15 dollars.
B : OK. Here you are.

대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
questions.explanation: Somi는 '두 병의 물(two bottles of water)'을 주문했으므로 물을 하나가 아닌 두 개를 주문했습니다. 따라서 '각 하나씩'이라는 표현은 잘못되었습니다.

options:
A: What would you like to order?
B: I'd like to order a strawberry cake.
A: Is it for or to go?
B: It's for here, please.

A: Is it for here or to go?
B: It's to go, please. Thank you.

A: What would you like to order?
B: I especially like the cheese Kimbap.

A: What would you like to order?
B: I want to get 7 cups of smoothie.
questions.question: 다음 대화 중 가장 자연스럽지 않은 것을 고르시오.
questions.explanation: 첫 번째 대화에서 "Is it for or to go?"는 문법적으로 불완전합니다. 정확한 표현은 "Is it for here or to go?"입니다. 세 번째 선택지의 "I especially like the cheese Kimbap"도 부자연스럽긴 하지만, 가장 명백한 오류는 첫 번째의 문법 오류입니다.

options: Is it for here or to go?
OK, then will that be all?
What would you like to order?
Would you like anything to drink?
questions.question:
다음 대화의 빈칸 (C)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말은?

M: Welcome to Sandwich Place.
_______________(A)_______________
G: I'd like to have a hamburger, and my sister will have a chicken sandwich.
M: _______________(B)_______________
G: Yes, two bottles of water, please.
M: _______________(C)_______________
G: No, I'd like to order one salad.
M: _______________(D)_______________
G: It's for here, please.
M: _______________(E)_______________
G: OK, here you are.
questions.explanation: (C) 위에서 G가 음료를 주문했으므로, 이제 다른 것을 더 주문할지 확인하는 "OK, then will that be all?"이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question:
[대화]
Haein : Hello. (A)What would you like to order?
Yumi : I want a hot dog and one milk, please.
Haein : Would you like anything else?
Yumi : No, thank you.
Haein : For here or to go?
Yumi : To go, please. Thank you.

(A)와 동일한 의미로 대체할 수 있는 표현은?
questions.explanation: "What would you like to order?"는 고객이 주문할 준비가 되었는지를 묻는 "Are you ready to order?"와 동일한 의미입니다.

options: Madeleines are Simon's favorite comfort food.
A madeleine is a kind of cake.
Most of French people especially enjoy madeleines with a cup of tea.
When Simon's grandmother bakes madeleines, the kitchen is full of sweet smells.
Simon wants to share his grandmother's special recipe for orange madeleines.
questions.question:
[지문]
Simon from France
I have many comfort foods, but I love madeleines the most. (A) A madeleine is a small cake that looks like a sea shell. (B) People in France enjoy madeleines as an afternoon snack. My grandmother always makes me madeleines when I visit her. (C) Then the kitchen is filled with a sweet smell. I especially like eating her orange madeleines with a cup of tea. (D) Every time I see or smell madeleines, I think of my grandmother. (E)

Let me share my grandmother's special recipe with you so that you can make orange madeleines, too. Maybe madeleines will become a comfort food for you!

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
questions.explanation: 글에서 "I especially like eating her orange madeleines with a cup of tea"라고 했으므로, 이는 Simon 개인의 선호도이지 "Most of French people"(대부분의 프랑스 사람들)이 그러하다는 내용이 아닙니다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Simon from France
I have many comfort foods, but I love madeleines the most. (A) A madeleine is a small cake that looks like a sea shell. (B) People in France enjoy madeleines as an afternoon snack. My grandmother always makes me madeleines when I visit her. (C) Then the kitchen is filled with a sweet smell. I especially like eating her orange madeleines with a cup of tea. (D) Every time I see or smell madeleines, I think of my grandmother. (E)

Let me share my grandmother's special recipe with you so that you can make orange madeleines, too. Maybe madeleines will become a comfort food for you!

윗글의 흐름상 다음 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 위치는?

They taste best when they come right out of the oven.
questions.explanation: 이 문장은 마들렌의 맛에 대한 설명이므로, (D) 이후 그리고 레시피를 공유하기 전인 위치에 있어야 자연스러운 흐름을 유지합니다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Grandma's Special Recipe: Orange Madeleines
You need: 1 cup of flour, 2/3 cup of sugar, 2 eggs, some orange peel, 1/4 cup of butter, 1/8 teaspoon of salt

(1) Melt the butter and let it cool.
(2) Put the eggs, sugar, and salt ___ⓐ___ a bowl and beat.
(3) Add the flour to the bowl and mix.
(4) Add the butter and orange peel to the mixture and mix.
(5) Pour the mixture ___ⓑ___ the madeleine pan.
(6) Bake in the oven ___ⓒ___ 10 to 15 minutes.

빈칸 ⓐ~ⓒ에 들어갈 적절한 단어가 바르게 나열된 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓐ: 'Put ~ in a bowl'은 "그릇 안에 넣다"는 의미로 'in'을 사용합니다. ⓑ: 'Pour ~ into the pan'은 "팬 안으로 붓다"는 의미로 'into'를 사용합니다. ⓒ: 'Bake for 10 to 15 minutes'는 "10~15분 동안 굽다"는 의미로 'for'를 사용합니다.

options: I took a taxi so that I was late for school.
I was late for school so that I took a taxi.
I was late for school because I took a taxi.
I took a taxi so that I wouldn't be late for school.
I didn't take a taxi so that I was late for school.
questions.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 올바르게 나타내는 것은?

나는 학교에 늦지 않도록 택시를 탔다.
questions.explanation: "~하지 않도록"은 부정적인 목적을 나타내므로 "so that I wouldn't be late"라는 표현이 정확합니다. (4번)는 "나는 학교에 늦지 않도록 택시를 탔다"는 원문의 의미를 올바르게 반영합니다.

options: disappear: to become possible to see or find
stable: staying the same, with no big changes or problems
professional: doing a sport or activity for money, as a job
lead: to show someone the way, by going in front of him or her
satisfy: to make someone feel happy, by doing what he or she wants
questions.question: 다음 단어의 설명으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.explanation: "disappear"는 "더 이상 보이지 않게 되다" 또는 "사라지다"라는 의미입니다. 주어진 설명 "to become possible to see or find"는 반대 의미의 "appear"의 정의입니다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Comfort food is food that makes you feel good when you are sad, angry, or stressed out. It can also make you think of happy moments from the past. It satisfies not only the stomach but also the heart. Comfort foods differ around the world. Let's see what comfort foods our international readers enjoy.

Jessica from USA

(ⓐ) My comfort food is chicken soup. (ⓑ) In the USA, people eat this soup when they have a cold. (ⓒ) When I was a small child, I caught a very bad cold. (ⓓ) My father made me a bowl of chicken soup so that I could get well. (ⓔ) It was also very tasty. Now, when I catch a cold, I eat chicken soup.

윗글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 다음 문장이 들어갈 가장 적절한 곳은?

The hot soup warmed my body, and I slowly started to feel better.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 아버지가 만든 수프를 먹은 후의 신체 반응을 설명합니다. (ⓓ) "My father made me a bowl of chicken soup so that I could get well." 직후에 위치하는 것이 자연스러운 흐름입니다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Comfort food is food that makes you ㉮______ good when you are sad, angry, or stressed out. It can also make you ㉯______ of happy moments from the past. It satisfies not only the stomach but also the heart. Comfort foods differ around the world. Let's see ㉰______ comfort foods our international readers enjoy.

윗글의 빈칸 ㉮, ㉯, ㉰에 들어갈 말을 순서대로 바르게 나열한 것은?
questions.explanation: ㉮: "makes you feel good"는 사역동사 make 뒤에 원형동사가 오므로 "feel"입니다. ㉯: "make you think of"는 "~을 생각하게 하다"는 의미로 "think"를 사용합니다. ㉰: "see what comfort foods"는 "어떤 편안한 음식들을 보다"는 의미로 "what"을 사용합니다.

options: Cassava is a kind of fruit.
Maria buys her friends chips often.
Maria can make cassava chips herself.
Cassava chips are Brazilians' favorite food.
Eating cassava chips makes Maria get out of stress.
questions.question:
[지문]
Maria From Brazil

In Brazil, there are many dishes ⓐthat made with cassava, a vegetable ⓑsimilar to a potato. I love cassava chips ⓒthe most. ⓓOnce when I had a bad day at school and felt stressed out, my best friend bought me a bag of cassava chips.

When I started to eat the chips, my stress suddenly disappeared. The crisp sound of eating chips made me feel better. Now, ⓔwhenever I'm stressed out, I eat cassava chips. Then I feel good again!

윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것을 고르시오.
questions.explanation: 글에서 "When I started to eat the chips, my stress suddenly disappeared."와 "whenever I'm stressed out, I eat cassava chips. Then I feel good again!"이라고 명시되어 있으므로, 카사바 칩을 먹으면 스트레스가 해소된다는 내용이 맞습니다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Maria From Brazil

In Brazil, there are many dishes ⓐthat made with cassava, a vegetable ⓑsimilar to a potato. I love cassava chips ⓒthe most. ⓓOnce when I had a bad day at school and felt stressed out, my best friend bought me a bag of cassava chips.

When I started to eat the chips, my stress suddenly disappeared. The crisp sound of eating chips made me feel better. Now, ⓔwhenever I'm stressed out, I eat cassava chips. Then I feel good again!

밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 문맥상 자연스럽지 않은 것은?
questions.explanation: "dishes that made with cassava"는 문법적으로 오류입니다. 정확한 표현은 "dishes that are made with cassava" 또는 "dishes made with cassava"이어야 합니다. 관계대명사 that 뒤에는 술어동사가 필요하므로 "are made"가 필요합니다.

questions.question:
빈칸 ⓐ~ⓔ를 채울 때 한 번도 쓰이지 않는 단어는?

(A) Add the flour ___ⓐ___ the bowl and mix.
(B) Pour the mixture ___ⓑ___ the madeleine pan.
(C) Put the eggs, sugar, and salt ___ⓒ___ a bowl and beat.
(D) Add the butter and orange peel ___ⓓ___ the mixture and mix.
(E) Bake in the oven ___ⓔ___ 10 to 15 minutes.
questions.explanation: ⓐ는 'to' (add ~ to), ⓑ는 'into' (pour ~ into), ⓒ는 'in' (in a bowl), ⓓ는 'to' (add ~ to), ⓔ는 'for' (for 10 to 15 minutes)이 올바른 전치사이다. 'at'은 한 번도 사용되지 않는다.

questions.question:
Madeleines 만드는 과정에서 (가) 단계 이후의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

(가) Melt the butter and let it cool.
questions.explanation: 요리 과정의 논리적 순서: 달걀, 설탕, 소금을 섞기(C) → 밀가루 추가(A) → 버터와 오렌지 껍질 추가(D) → 팬에 붓기(B) → 구우기(E)

questions.question:
[지문]
In Brazil, there are many dishes that are made (A) cassava, a vegetable similar (B) a potato. I love cassava chips the most. Once when I had a bad day at school and felt stressed out, my best friend bought me a bag of cassava chips.

When I started to eat the chips, my stress suddenly disappeared. The crisp sound of eating chips made me feel better. Now, every time I'm stressed out, I eat cassava chips. Then I feel good again!

위 글에서 밑줄 친 every time과 의미가 가장 유사한 것은?
questions.explanation: 'every time I'm stressed out'은 '스트레스받을 때마다'라는 의미이며, 'whenever'는 '~할 때마다'라는 의미로 동일한 뜻이다.

questions.question:
[지문]
In Brazil, there are many dishes that are made (A) cassava, a vegetable similar (B) a potato. I love cassava chips the most. Once when I had a bad day at school and felt stressed out, my best friend bought me a bag of cassava chips.

When I started to eat the chips, my stress suddenly disappeared. The crisp sound of eating chips made me feel better. Now, every time I'm stressed out, I eat cassava chips. Then I feel good again!

위 글의 괄호 (A), (B)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말의 조합은?
questions.explanation: 'made with cassava' (cassava로 만든)와 'similar to a potato' (감자와 유사한)이 올바른 전치사 조합이다.

questions.question:
[지문]
My comfort food is chicken soup. In the USA, people eat this soup when they have a cold. When I was a small child, I caught a very bad cold. My father made me a bowl of chicken soup so that I could set well. The hot soup warmed my body, and I slowly started to feel better. It was also very tasty. Now, when I catch a cold, I eat chicken soup.

When do people eat chicken soup in the USA?
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'In the USA, people eat this soup when they have a cold.'라고 명시되어 있다.

comfort food는 기분 좋을 때 먹는 음식이다.
comfort food는 과거의 행복한 순간을 떠올리게 할 수 있다.
전 세계 모든 사람들은 comfort food가 같다.
questions.question:
[지문]
Comfort food is food that makes you feel good when you are sad, angry, or stressed out. It can also make you think of happy moments from the past. It satisfies not only the stomach but also the heart. Comfort foods differ around the world. Let's see what comfort foods our international readers enjoy.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것을 고르시오.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'It can also make you think of happy moments from the past.'라고 명시되어 있다. 다른 선택지들은 지문 내용과 맞지 않는다.

options: disappear : to become possible to see or find
satisfy : to work hard in order to achieve something
quantity : an amount that you can measure or count
expert : the group of people watching or listening to a play, film or public meeting
questions.question: 다음 중 단어와 영영풀이가 바르게 연결된 것은?
questions.explanation: quantity는 '측정하거나 셀 수 있는 양'이라는 의미로 올바르게 정의되었다. 다른 보기들: comfort(편안함), disappear(사라지다), satisfy(만족시키다), expert(전문가)의 정의는 모두 잘못되었다.

options: The novel almost made me cry.
Can you make me a sandwich now?
Eating chocolate makes me feel good.
The teacher made them write the report.
That coat makes you look much younger.
questions.question: 밑줄 친 단어의 쓰임이 나머지와 다른 것은?
questions.explanation: ①③④⑤는 'make + 목적어 + 동사원형(또는 형용사/명사)' 구조인 반면, ②는 'make + 목적어 + 명사' 구조로 '~를 만들어주다'라는 의미이다.

questions.question:
다음 문장들의 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 알맞은 단어가 순서대로 나열된 것은?

＊We had a lot of ___(A)___ last winter.
＊The pizza my mom made was very ___(B)___.
＊I felt very ___(C)___, so I couldn't open my eyes.
questions.explanation: (A) 'a lot of'는 명사를 필요로 하므로 'snowy'(형용사)가 아닌 물질명사이어야 하지만, 문맥상 '작년 겨울이 많이 눈이 내렸다'는 의미로 snowy가 맞다. (B) 'very'는 형용사/부사를 수식하므로 'salty'(형용사) (C) 'felt'는 연결동사이므로 'sleepy'(형용사)

questions.question:
[지문]
In Brazil, there are many dishes that are made with cassava, a vegetable similar to a potato. ⓐI love cassava chips the most. ⓑOnce when I had a bad day at school, my best friend bought a bag of cassava chips for me. ⓒWhen I started to eat the chips, my stress suddenly appeared. ⓓI felt much better after eating cassava chips. ⓔNow, every time I feel bad, I eat cassava chips. Then I feel good again!

글의 흐름으로 볼 때 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 가장 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓒ에서 'my stress suddenly appeared'는 논리적으로 맞지 않다. 문맥상 '스트레스가 사라졌다(disappeared)'가 올바른 표현이다. 원본 텍스트에서도 'my stress suddenly disappeared'로 되어 있다.
